This article details the list of women's singles [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] tournaments [[tennis]] champions. Some major changes have taken place in history and have affected the number of titles that have been won by various players. These have included the opening of the French national championships to international players in 1925, the elimination of the challenge round in 1922, and the admission of professional players in 1968 (the start of the [[History of tennis#Open Era|Open Era]]). Since then, 63 women have won at least one grand slam.<ref>ESPN Sports Almanac 2006, page 814</ref><ref>World Book Encyclopedia 2008 T p166a</ref><ref>Compton Encyclopedia 1975 ST p301</ref><ref>Concord Encyclopedia</ref><ref>CBS Sports "[http://www.cbssports.com/tennis/history/slams/women] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204095407/http://www.cbssports.com/tennis/history/slams/women|date=2009-02-04}}"</ref><ref>Top End Sports "[http://www.topendsports.com/events/tennis-grand-slam/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090710195114/http://www.topendsports.com/events/tennis-grand-slam/|date=2009-07-10}}"</ref><ref>[https://www.usatoday.com/sports/tennis/00wim/sampras2.htm] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110122235012/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/tennis/00wim/sampras2.htm|date=2011-01-22}}"</ref><ref>Tennis 28 Slams "[http://www.tennis28.com/slams/wins_alltime.html] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090722022238/http://www.tennis28.com/slams/wins_alltime.html|date=2009-07-22}}"</ref>

All of these tournaments have been listed based on the modern definition of a tennis major, rather than when they were officially recognized by the [[ILTF]]. The [[Australian Open#History|Australian]], [[French Open#History|French Championships]], and [[US Open (tennis)#History|U.S.]] tournaments were officially recognized by the ILTF in 1924, though the French Championships were not played in 1924 because of the Olympics. The [[United States Lawn Tennis Association]] (USLTA) had several grievances with the ILTF and refused to join when it was formed in 1913.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Robertson, Max |title=The Encyclopedia of Tennis |publisher=Viking Press |publication-date=1974 |pages=28–30}}</ref>

From 1913 to 1923 there were three official championships recognized by the ILTF:
* [[World Grass Court Championships]] – Wimbledon.
* [[World Hard Court Championships]], held in Paris on clay courts.
* [[World Covered Court Championships]], held in Europe on an indoor wood surface.

During that same time period the USLTA recognized the U.S. National Championships and did not recognize any world championship.
* [[US Open (tennis)|U.S. National Championships]], held in New York on grass.

== Grand Slam achievements ==
{{Main|Grand Slam (tennis)}}

These are players who achieved some form of a tennis [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]]. They include a Grand Slam, non-calendar year Grand Slam, Career Grand Slam, Career Golden Slam, and Career Super Slam. No player has won a single season [[List of women's wheelchair tennis champions#Super Slam|Super Slam]]. The tennis [[Open Era]] began in 1968, after the [[1968 Australian Open|Australian Open]] and before the [[1968 French Open|French Open]].
